evidence.excerpt: Returns. Last holiday season. Buy online, return in store.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Trigger of the evaluation: omnichannel returns problem.

evidence.excerpt: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Concrete failure in store returns; stated as fact by rep.

evidence.excerpt: they'd just launched a loyalty program that was supposed to work everywhere and didn't, because store and web were two different customer records.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Loyalty program broken by split customer records.

evidence.excerpt: Their COO, Angela, apparently stood in a store on December 27th watching the returns queue. That's the story everybody there tells.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Hedged with 'apparently'; secondhand lore, rep not present. Shows COO Angela's personal stake.

evidence.label: opinion

contradictions.what: Rep named Raj as final decider, then said Angela signed with Adyen and revised to 'Probably Angela'.
Rep says they were ahead and had won the web side, yet 'knew on the drive home' it was lost; being ahead rests on Raj, not Angela.
Rep claims Raj was contact all the way, yet met the actual signer Angela only once; the real decider was barely engaged.
Rep says Raj wanted us, but the store workshop that sank the deal came from Angela's team, outside Raj's control.
Our pitch said unified platform with the line disappeared, yet customer wanted proof at the till and never used our wording.

dodges.question: What did you say? (to Bev's step-by-step return question)
dodges.what: Answered 'I described it,' implying no demo; later admitted never showed it.

dodges.question: So who made the final call?
dodges.what: Hedged with 'Probably' and 'I think' after earlier confidently naming Raj.
